journey.title: Opt out of reminders with the keyboard after choosing Text message
journey.goal: Arrowing from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field that no longer applies

functionalJourney.title: Switch reminder channel with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Choosing Email then Text message shows only the mobile number field

guards.title: Choose Email with the keyboard and enter an address
guards.goal: Selecting Email reveals the email address field and the address is kept

plan.root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility for radios with data-aria-controls on click events; it does not respond to changes in checked state via keyboard navigation, leaving conditionals visible when a radio without controls (e.g., opt‑out) is selected.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a change listener to the radios module that invokes setAttributes on all radios with controls whenever any radio's checked state changes, ensuring conditionals are shown/hidden based on the newly selected radio.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now navigate the radio group with arrow keys and see dependent fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Possible duplicate execution of setAttributes when both click and change events fire for the same interaction.
If another script depends on the change event not being fired, adding the listener could cause unintended side effects.
Minimal performance overhead from traversing the radio list on each change event.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting each radio option via keyboard updates the visibility of its associated conditional field correctly.
Verify that clicking a radio option continues to work as before.
Verify that ARIA attributes (aria-controls, aria-expanded) are correctly updated on both click and keyboard selection.
Ensure no regression in existing visual behavior for mouse users.

plan.root_cause: The radios component only responds to click events, not keyboard-driven change events. When a user navigates with arrow keys to the opt-out radio (which lacks aria-controls), the previously selected radio's conditional field remains visible because no change handler updates aria-expanded and visibility for all radios with aria-controls.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a change event listener that invokes setAttributes on every radio with aria-controls whenever any radio's checked state changes. This ensures conditionals are shown/hidden correctly for both mouse and keyboard interactions.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate the radio group with arrow keys and see dependent fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Possible duplicate execution of setAttributes when both click and change events fire for the same interaction.
If another script depends on the change event not being observed, adding the listener could cause unintended side effects.
Minimal performance overhead from traversing the radio list on each change event.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting each radio option via keyboard updates the visibility of its associated conditional field correctly.
Verify that clicking a radio option continues to work as before.
Verify that ARIA attributes (aria-controls, aria-expanded) are correctly updated on both click and keyboard selection.
Ensure no regression in existing visual behavior for mouse users.

plan.root_cause: The radios component only responds to click events within its own module. When keyboard navigation selects a radio in a different module but same radio group (shared name='reminder'), the original module receives no event, leaving its conditional field visible incorrectly.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a document-level change event listener that detects when any radio in the same name group changes, then updates all conditionals in this module by calling setAttributes on each radio with aria-controls.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all reminder options (including across visual groups) and see dependent fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Double execution of setAttributes when both click and change events fire for the same interaction (idempotent, low risk).
Document-level listener catches changes from any radio on the page; mitigated by name check.
If modules are dynamically destroyed, document listeners remain (not an issue for static pages).
